preloginPage.title: Trustworthy AI Evaluation Test
preloginPage.taiExplainContent: Artificial Intelligence (AI) technology has gradually gained importance across various fields in society in recent years. To enhance the trustworthiness of AI technology in applications, the European Union released the Ethics Guidelines for Trustworthy AI in 2019. In 2023, Taiwan's Ministry of Digital Affairs established the AI Product and System Evaluation Center to develop evaluation projects for building a domestic AI product and system evaluation framework.
preloginPage.purposeContent: This evaluation form is based on the EU Ethics Guidelines for Trustworthy AI and the evaluation projects proposed by Taiwan's Ministry of Digital Affairs. It designs 11 trustworthy AI ethical self-assessment indicators to provide AI model developers and potential users with a checklist during deployment, aiming to meet trustworthy AI ethical standards.
preloginPage.accuracyContent: The degree to which AI judgments are close to the real situation
preloginPage.reliabilityContent: When facing different types of interference or abnormal situations, the AI model maintains moderate sensitivity without being overly sensitive, ensuring stable performance
preloginPage.securityContent: If the AI system fails, it will not cause adverse impacts or harm to the surrounding environment or stakeholders (such as users and the public)
preloginPage.toughnessContent: AI systems and related equipment can adapt to different environments, requirements, and conditions, flexibly adjusting and expanding to meet changing needs and challenges
preloginPage.transparencyContent: AI system users can trace the data, algorithms, or rules used when AI makes judgments or decisions
preloginPage.responsibilityContent: When AI systems cause unexpected negative impacts, there must be supervision mechanisms or responsible units or individuals
preloginPage.interpretabilityContent: The decision logic of AI (i.e., the causal relationship between data input and decision results) can be clearly described and presented, helping users and stakeholders better understand the reasons behind AI decisions
preloginPage.autonomyContent: During interactions between AI system users and AI, users can maintain sufficient autonomy without overly relying on AI judgments or decisions
preloginPage.privacyContent: The use of AI systems will not infringe on personal privacy
preloginPage.fairnessContent: AI systems treat different groups equally when making judgments or decisions, avoiding unfair situations
preloginPage.informationSecurityContent: To prevent external environmental intrusion and damage to AI models, and to protect data security during training and testing

law.intro: The following outlines the legal requirements that AI systems must comply with before, during, and after the modeling process, including personal data protection, intellectual property, cybersecurity, open data, and AI responsibility.

item1.title: 1️⃣ Legality of Personal Data Collection, Processing, and Use
item1.law: Relevant Regulations: PDPA Article 6, Article 9 Paragraph 2 Subparagraph 2
item1.point1: Data collection must have a legitimate and specific purpose.
item1.point2: Sensitive personal data requires meeting legal exceptions.
item1.point3: Legality and necessity must be confirmed before AI training.

item2.title: 2️⃣ Obligation to Inform Before Collection (Including Indirect Collection)
item2.point1: Data subjects must be informed of purpose, usage, retention period, and rights.
item2.point2: Indirectly obtained data must also be properly notified.

item3.title: 3️⃣ Restrictions on Disclosure of De-identified Data
item3.point1: Data not fully de-identified is still considered personal data.
item3.point2: Re-identification of individuals must be prevented.

item4.title: 4️⃣ Rights of Data Subjects
item4.point1: Provide rights to withdraw consent, access, correct, delete, and stop usage.
item4.point2: Systems must provide an opt-out mechanism.
item4.point3: Access control and data handling procedures must be established.

item5.title: 5️⃣ Personal Data Management and Incident Handling
item5.point1: Establish a personal data management system.
item5.point2: Maintain access logs, audit trails, and evidence preservation.
item5.point3: Implement incident response and notification mechanisms.

item6.title: 6️⃣ Cross-border Data Transfer Regulations
item6.point1: Cross-border transfers must comply with Taiwan regulations and international standards (e.g., GDPR).
item6.point2: Data protection agreements must be signed with overseas partners.

ip.title: II. Intellectual Property and Open Source

item1.title: 1️⃣ Software is Protected Under Copyright Law
item1.law: Relevant Regulations: Copyright Act Article 5 Paragraph 1 Subparagraph 10

item3.title: 3️⃣ IP Ownership in Collaboration and Development Agreements

opendata.title: III. Open Data Requirements
opendata.point1: Establish data quality review and update mechanisms.
opendata.point3: Personal data within open data remains subject to PDPA.

responsibility.title: IV. AI Responsibility and Liability
responsibility.point1: AI must not replace human decision-making.
responsibility.point2: Public liability is borne by the using agency.

userRights.title: V. User Rights and Transparency
userRights.point1: Inform users of model accuracy, limitations, and risks.
userRights.point2: Prevent users from over-relying on AI.
userRights.point3: Provide channels for user inquiries and understanding.

cybersecurity.title: VI. Cybersecurity Regulations
cybersecurity.point1: Conduct assessments of model vulnerabilities and attack risks.
cybersecurity.point2: Establish cybersecurity management and access control.
cybersecurity.point3: Implement incident reporting and remediation procedures.
